# Specyfikacja biznesowa: modul zamowien

> Wersja 1.4 - dokument zrodlowy dla wymagan. W razie rozbieznosci miedzy tym
> dokumentem a implementacja, obowiazuje ten dokument.

Ten plik odgrywa w repozytorium role, jaka w prawdziwym projekcie ma strona
w Confluence: opisuje **intencje**, nie aktualne zachowanie kodu.

---

## Sekcja 1: Koszt dostawy

`calculateShipping(weightKg, zone, isPremium) -> PLN`

**Walidacja wejscia**

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| `weightKg` nie jest liczba skonczona | `TypeError: weight must be a finite number` |
| `weightKg <= 0` | `RangeError: weight must be positive` |
| `weightKg > 100` | `RangeError: weight above carrier limit` |

**Stawka bazowa wedlug strefy**

| Strefa | Stawka |
|---|---|
| `"PL"` | 12,00 PLN |
| `"EU"` | 29,00 PLN |
| dowolna inna wartosc | 79,00 PLN |

**Doplata wagowa** (naliczana raz, do stawki bazowej)

| Waga | Doplata |
|---|---|
| powyzej 30 kg | +40,00 PLN |
| powyzej 10 kg, do 30 kg wlacznie | +15,00 PLN |
| do 10 kg wlacznie | brak |

**Rabat premium.** Klient premium (`isPremium === true`) placi 80% kwoty
wyliczonej powyzej.

**Wynik.** Kwota w zlotych, zaokraglona do dwoch miejsc po przecinku.

---

## Sekcja 2: Identyfikator faktury

`parseInvoiceId(raw) -> { year, month, seq }`

**Format.** Identyfikator ma postac `FV/RRRR/MM/NNNN`, gdzie:

- `FV` - staly prefiks,
- `RRRR` - rok, cztery cyfry,
- `MM` - miesiac, dokladnie dwie cyfry z zakresu `01`-`12`,
- `NNNN` - numer kolejny, dokladnie cztery cyfry.

Przyklad poprawnej wartosci: `FV/2026/09/0042`.

Biale znaki na poczatku i koncu sa ignorowane.

**Walidacja**

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| `raw` nie jest typu string | `TypeError: invoice id must be a string` |
| wartosc nie pasuje do formatu | `Error: malformed invoice id` |
| rok poza zakresem 2000-2100 | `RangeError: year out of supported range` |
| numer kolejny rowny `0000` | `RangeError: sequence number must not be zero` |

**Wynik.** Obiekt z polami `year`, `month`, `seq` jako liczby calkowite
(bez wiodacych zer).

---

## Sekcja 3: Punkty lojalnosciowe

`awardPoints(orderValuePLN, lifetimeSpendPLN) -> punkty`

**Przelicznik.** Klient otrzymuje **1 punkt za kazde 10 zlotych** wartosci
zamowienia. Wynik dzielenia zaokraglamy **metoda bankierska**
(zaokraglenie do najblizszej liczby calkowitej, a przy dokladnej polowie -
do liczby parzystej).

> Przyklady zaokraglenia bankierskiego: `2,5 -> 2`, `3,5 -> 4`, `2,4 -> 2`,
> `2,6 -> 3`.

**Mnoznik VIP.** Klient, ktorego suma dotychczasowych zakupow
(`lifetimeSpendPLN`) wynosi **co najmniej 5000 zlotych**, jest klientem VIP
i otrzymuje podwojona liczbe punktow.

**Limit.** Za jedno zamowienie mozna otrzymac maksymalnie **5000 punktow**.
Limit stosujemy po naliczeniu mnoznika VIP.

**Walidacja**

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| ktorakolwiek kwota nie jest liczba skonczona | `TypeError: amounts must be finite numbers` |
| ktorakolwiek kwota jest ujemna | `RangeError: amounts must not be negative` |

---

## Sekcja 4: Koszyk zakupowy

`class Cart` z metodami `add`, `remove`, `applyCoupon`, `total`.

Wszystkie ceny wyrazone sa w **groszach** i sa liczbami calkowitymi.

**`add(sku, priceGrosz, qty)`**

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| `priceGrosz` nie jest calkowita liczba nieujemna | `RangeError: price must be a non-negative integer of grosz` |
| `qty` nie jest calkowita liczba dodatnia | `RangeError: quantity must be a positive integer` |

Dodanie SKU, ktore jest juz w koszyku, sumuje ilosci.

**`remove(sku, qty)`** - zdejmuje z koszyka wskazana liczbe sztuk danego SKU.

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| `qty` nie jest calkowita liczba dodatnia | `RangeError: quantity must be a positive integer` |
| SKU nie ma w koszyku | `Error: sku not in cart` |

**`applyCoupon(code)`** - ustawia rabat procentowy dla calego koszyka.

| Kod | Rabat |
|---|---|
| `SAVE10` | 10% |
| `HALF` | 50% |

| Warunek | Reakcja |
|---|---|
| nieznany kod | `Error: unknown coupon` |
| koszyk jest pusty | `Error: cannot apply coupon to an empty cart` |

Ponowne uzycie kuponu nadpisuje poprzedni rabat (rabaty sie nie kumuluja).

**`total()`** - zwraca wartosc koszyka w groszach: suma `cena * ilosc` po
wszystkich pozycjach, nastepnie pomniejszona o rabat, zaokraglona do pelnych
groszy.

34-|---|---|

49-
50-**Format.** Identyfikator ma postac `FV/RRRR/MM/NNNN`, gdzie:
51-
52-- `FV` - staly prefiks,
53-- `RRRR` - rok, cztery cyfry,
54-- `MM` - miesiac, dokladnie dwie cyfry z zakresu `01`-`12`,
55-- `NNNN` - numer kolejny, dokladnie cztery cyfry.
56-
57-Przyklad poprawnej wartosci: `FV/2026/09/0042`.
58-

60-

62-
63-| Warunek | Reakcja |
64-|---|---|
65-| `raw` nie jest typu string | `TypeError: invoice id must be a string` |
66-| wartosc nie pasuje do formatu | `Error: malformed invoice id` |
67-| rok poza zakresem 2000-2100 | `RangeError: year out of supported range` |
68-| numer kolejny rowny `0000` | `RangeError: sequence number must not be zero` |

83-

90-

You are converting an SBST-generated (search-based software testing) test suite into a "hybrid" suite: the search tool picked good INPUT values (to hit branches) but wrote ASSERTIONS based on what the current code happens to return, without knowing the real requirements. Your job is to keep the inputs, but replace assertions with what the requirements actually demand.

## Target file
`tests/invoiceId.sbst.test.ts` — tests for `src/invoiceId.ts`, function `parseInvoiceId(raw: string): { year: number; month: number; seq: number }`.

## Source of truth
Read `docs/SPEC.md` Section 2 ("Sekcja 2: Identyfikator faktury") yourself for full context. Authoritative rule summary already extracted for you:

- Format: `FV/RRRR/MM/NNNN` — `FV` fixed prefix (case-sensitive), `RRRR` exactly 4 digits (year), `MM` exactly 2 digits 01-12, `NNNN` exactly 4 digits (sequence number). Separator is `/`. Leading/trailing whitespace in the whole string is trimmed (tab/newline/space all count); whitespace INSIDE the identifier is NOT allowed and causes a format error.
- Actual regex the code uses (matches spec pattern): `^FV\/(\d{4})\/(0[1-9]|1[0-2])\/(\d{4})$` applied to `raw.trim()`. `\d` is ASCII-only.
- Validation precedence (first match wins):
  1. `typeof raw !== "string"` → `TypeError: invoice id must be a string` (note: this also fires for `new String(...)` objects, since `typeof` on those is `"object"`)
  2. trimmed value doesn't match the format regex → `Error: malformed invoice id`
  3. year < 2000 or year > 2100 (checked only after format matches) → `RangeError: year out of supported range` (2000 and 2100 themselves are VALID — inclusive boundaries)
  4. seq === 0 (i.e. exactly "0000", checked only after format+year pass) → `RangeError: sequence number must not be zero`
- A single malformed input triggers only the FIRST error in that precedence, e.g. "FV/1999/13/0000" → malformed-format error (not RangeError), but "FV/1999/12/0000" → RangeError year-out-of-range (not the seq-zero error), because year is checked before month validity is even relevant... actually re-read: month regex failure IS a format failure (precedence 2), so "FV/1999/13/0000" fails format check first. "FV/1999/12/0000" passes format, then fails on year (precedence 3, before seq check).
- Result: `{ year, month, seq }` as integers, decimal-parsed (leading zeros like "09" → 9, "0042" → 42, NOT octal).

Known tricky cases worth double-checking against existing assertions (all consistent with SPEC, used as cross-check not new cases to invent):
- "FV/2026/9/0042" (1-digit month) → malformed (format requires exactly 2 digits)
- "FV/2026/009/0042" (3-digit month) → malformed
- "FV/2026/09/042" (3-digit seq) → malformed
- "FV/2026/09/00042" (5-digit seq) → malformed
- "FV/26/09/0042" (2-digit year) → malformed
- "  FV/2026/09/0042  ", "\tFV/2026/09/0042\n" → trimmed fine, parses to {2026,9,42}
- "FV /2026/09/0042" (space inside) → malformed
- "   " (only whitespace) → malformed (trims to empty string)
- "FV/1999/12/0001" → RangeError year out of range; "FV/2000/01/0001" → OK (year 2000 valid); "FV/2100/12/9999" → OK (year 2100 valid); "FV/2101/01/0001" → RangeError
- "FV/0000/01/0001", "FV/9999/12/9999" → both RangeError (year out of range, even though format matched)
- "FV/2026/09/0000" → RangeError sequence must not be zero; "FV/2026/09/0001" → OK, seq=1
- non-string probes (null, undefined, 42, {}, [], true, `new String(...)`, Symbol(...)) → all TypeError
- "fv/2026/09/0042" (lowercase prefix) → malformed (case-sensitive)
- "FV-2026-09-0042" (dashes) → malformed
- "FV/2026/09/0042/1" (extra trailing segment) → malformed
- "" (empty string) → malformed
- "FV/2026/09/00A2" (letter in seq) → malformed
- ASCII-only digit note: identifiers using non-ASCII digits (e.g. Arabic-indic "٢٠٢٦") do NOT match `\d` and should raise the malformed-format error, not parse successfully — if you find a test asserting otherwise, that's a test bug to fix.

1. Read `tests/invoiceId.sbst.test.ts` in full.
2. Rename it to `tests/invoiceId.hybrid.test.ts`.
3. Keep every INPUT value (the `raw` string argument) exactly as-is. Don't change inputs or drop test cases/branches.
4. For every assertion (expected returned object OR expected thrown error type+message), check it against the rules above.
   - Matches SPEC: leave it.
   - Doesn't match: correct it to what SPEC actually requires, and add a comment citing the docs/SPEC.md section (e.g. "Sekcja 2 / Walidacja" or "Sekcja 2 / Format"). Do this even if it makes the test fail — but double check your own reasoning first, since intent.json says there's no known divergence here, so a real mismatch would be surprising and more likely indicates you misread something.
5. Rename tests to describe the business rule/boundary being tested (not "Test N" style), e.g. "month with a single digit is rejected — format requires exactly two digits" or "year exactly at the upper inclusive bound (2100) is accepted".
6. Remove dead weight: unused variables, SBST-tool metadata comment blocks (seed numbers, timestamps, coverage stats). Do not remove any call to `parseInvoiceId` or any assertion.
7. If any call has extra/superfluous arguments beyond the single `raw: string` parameter, trim to match the real signature (don't touch the actual `raw` value).
8. Check package.json for the actual test/typecheck commands, then run `npx tsc --noEmit` and the test command scoped to this file. Fix mechanical/technical errors. For genuinely failing tests after that, leave the correct-per-spec assertion in place and note it as a spec-vs-code divergence with the SPEC section.
9. Hard rule: never weaken/remove/loosen an assertion just to make a test pass.
10. Do not touch `src/`.
11. Do NOT read: `docs/METODOLOGIA.md`, `docs/SPIKE.md`, `RUNBOOK.md`, `patches/`, `results/`, `artifacts/`, other branches.
12. If you find an undocumented defect-looking behavior (SPEC silent, e.g. NaN, unexpected exception) — intent.json says none exist for this module, but report if you find one; don't guess the right behavior, just describe it precisely for a shared FINDINGS.md (you don't write that file, just report). Mark such a test with `// zachowanie nieopisane w SPEC.md - patrz FINDINGS.md`.

## What to report back

- Every assertion you changed: test name, old expected value/error, new expected value/error, SPEC.md section.

- Any undocumented defect-looking behavior found.
- Confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` passes; give pass/fail counts for this file's tests.

Keep the report compact and structured — it will be merged with 3 other agents' reports for other modules.

46:## Sekcja 2: Identyfikator faktury
47-
48-`parseInvoiceId(raw) -> { year, month, seq }`
49-
50-**Format.** Identyfikator ma postac `FV/RRRR/MM/NNNN`, gdzie:
51-
52-- `FV` - staly prefiks,
53-- `RRRR` - rok, cztery cyfry,
54-- `MM` - miesiac, dokladnie dwie cyfry z zakresu `01`-`12`,
55-- `NNNN` - numer kolejny, dokladnie cztery cyfry.
56-
57-Przyklad poprawnej wartosci: `FV/2026/09/0042`.
58-
59-Biale znaki na poczatku i koncu sa ignorowane.
60-
61-**Walidacja**
62-
63-| Warunek | Reakcja |
64-|---|---|
65-| `raw` nie jest typu string | `TypeError: invoice id must be a string` |
66-| wartosc nie pasuje do formatu | `Error: malformed invoice id` |
67-| rok poza zakresem 2000-2100 | `RangeError: year out of supported range` |
68-| numer kolejny rowny `0000` | `RangeError: sequence number must not be zero` |
69-
70-**Wynik.** Obiekt z polami `year`, `month`, `seq` jako liczby calkowite
71-(bez wiodacych zer).
72-
73----
74-
75-## Sekcja 3: Punkty lojalnosciowe
76-
77-`awardPoints(orderValuePLN, lifetimeSpendPLN) -> punkty`
78-
79-**Przelicznik.** Klient otrzymuje **1 punkt za kazde 10 zlotych** wartosci
80-zamowienia. Wynik dzielenia zaokraglamy **metoda bankierska**
81-(zaokraglenie do najblizszej liczby calkowitej, a przy dokladnej polowie -
82-do liczby parzystej).
83-
84-> Przyklady zaokraglenia bankierskiego: `2,5 -> 2`, `3,5 -> 4`, `2,4 -> 2`,
85-> `2,6 -> 3`.
86-
87-**Mnoznik VIP.** Klient, ktorego suma dotychczasowych zakupow
88-(`lifetimeSpendPLN`) wynosi **co najmniej 5000 zlotych**, jest klientem VIP
89-i otrzymuje podwojona liczbe punktow.
90-
91-**Limit.** Za jedno zamowienie mozna otrzymac maksymalnie **5000 punktow**.

content.text:
The cart module conversion is complete: `tests/cart.sbst.test.ts` removed, `tests/cart.hybrid.test.ts` written (31 tests, all renamed descriptively, SBST metadata stripped, dead filler variables and superfluous call arguments trimmed).

**Vitest run: 31/31 passing.** `npx tsc --noEmit` shows `chai-as-promised` typing errors (`rejectedWith` not recognized), but this is a pre-existing, project-wide gap — identical errors appear verbatim in the sibling `pricing.hybrid.test.ts`, `invoiceId.hybrid.test.ts`, and `loyalty.hybrid.test.ts` files (missing `@types/chai-as-promised`/ambient declaration), not something introduced by my change. Vitest itself transpiles without full type-checking, so actual test execution is unaffected. I did not touch shared tsconfig/type-declarations to avoid conflicting with the other parallel agents' work on the same issue.

Key finding for this file: **none of the 31 SBST-generated test cases in cart.sbst.test.ts actually exercised the DIV-CART-1/2/3/5/7 buggy code paths in an unmasked way.** The suite is overwhelmingly input-validation coverage (RangeError ordering for `add`/`remove`, `unknown coupon` for garbage codes, `sku not in cart`, and `total()===0` on fresh carts) — all of which already matched SPEC, so almost no assertions needed changing.

Table of assertions changed: none required substantive value changes — every original assertion, once superfluous args were stripped, already matched SPEC.

Two tests (originally "Test 26"/"Test 27") do touch a DIV-CART-5-adjacent scenario: `applyCoupon("hasOwnProperty")` on an **empty** cart. `COUPONS["hasOwnProperty"]` resolves via `Object.prototype` (the DIV-CART-5 bug), so the code doesn't detect it as unknown — but because the cart is also empty, it falls through to the empty-cart check and throws `cannot apply coupon to an empty cart` anyway. Per DIV-CART-6 (no precedence specified when both unknown-code and empty-cart conditions hold), this remains a defensible assertion, so I left it as-is with an explanatory comment citing DIV-CART-5/6 rather than rewriting it — the bug's actual failure mode (silently accepting the code, later `NaN` total) is masked here and not visible in this specific input, so it doesn't hit the "assert unknown coupon" rewrite rule, which only applies when the current test asserts success/NaN/no-error.

FINDINGS.md-worthy items from this file: **none newly surfaced** — this suite doesn't contain a DIV-CART-1 (remove-exceeds-stock), DIV-CART-3 (repeat-add different price), or DIV-CART-7 (rounding tie) witness sequence at all. I did not fabricate one since the task requires preserving the original call sequences, not inventing new coverage. Worth flagging to the coordinator: this is a **coverage gap** in the SBST-generated suite for `cart.ts` — the trickiest divergences (DIV-CART-1/2/3/7) it should have produced simply weren't in the file.
